## c8e53a07acc8

**Reproduced teaching shortcut: the generator never teaches iteration over multiple templates.** Audited generator SHA-256: `312e7083ffb6ad87018ecca3b069d769236104e8e872605178cb9bc16c2af30f`; executed canonical rule hash: `559aa4d81a8f`. Across 30 source-bound generated cases (10 per band; seeds 7000–7009, 7100–7109, and 7200–7209), every input passed `self_check` and contained exactly one multicolor template. A Python mirror that intentionally processes only the first template matched the canonical Racket output on all 30/30 cases.

That shortcut is wrong on the authored task. The independent full Python mirror matched all five labeled canonical variant-0 pairs, while the first-template-only rival differed on canonical train pair 0 by 5 cells, test pair 0 by 22 cells, and test pair 1 by 16 cells. Those inputs contain two, three, and two multicolor templates respectively. The generator therefore supplies no counterexample to a shortcut that fails core canonical multi-template behavior.

The inherited battery independently reported 5 failed stages: missing `RULE_HASH` and inert axes, rule/source divergence, unreachable canonical palette sizes, override-contract failures, and active authority text divergence. These are additional source-bound findings, but the multi-template shortcut is the primary training-data defect.

Evidence and executable probe: `checks/audit/c8e53a07acc8/single-template-counterexample.json`, `checks/audit/c8e53a07acc8/probe_single_template.py`, `checks/audit/c8e53a07acc8/generated-inputs.json`, `checks/audit/c8e53a07acc8/generated-racket.json`, and `checks/audit/c8e53a07acc8/battery/`. No target file was modified.
